parsed.quote: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content, that have been placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026.
parsed.answer: Your deadline is 2 December 2026. Your text-generating system was placed on the EU market in March 2026, which is before 2 August 2026. Under the transitional rule that the Omnibus added as Article 111(4), you must take the steps needed to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026. That means marking outputs in a machine-readable format and making them detectable as artificially generated. AI systems first placed on the market on or after 2 August 2026 do not get this extra time.

parsed.answer: Article 50(1) is not covered by any of the earlier or later application dates in Article 113. It therefore falls under the general rule and applies from 2 August 2026. The Digital Omnibus proposals concerned other Article 50 transitional points, mainly 50(2), not the 50(1) date.

parsed.answer: The Commission must adopt these delegated acts by 2 August 2027, using the procedure in Article 97. The acts must say which Article 6(1) high-risk AI systems are covered, which requirements in Articles 9–15 and 17–25 may be limited, under what conditions, and how far. A limitation is only allowed where Union harmonisation legislation in Annex I Section A gives an equivalent or higher level of protection, and where the limitation does not lower the overall protection the Regulation provides. Article 2(13) was added by the Omnibus amendment.

parsed.quote: It shall apply from 2 August 2026.
parsed.answer: On 20 July 2026 the text in force was still the original Regulation 2024/1689. Under Article 113, the high-risk obligations for Annex III systems, including creditworthiness assessment and credit scoring (Annex III, point 5(b)), apply from 2 August 2026. However, the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) had already been adopted and published, according to secondary sources (law firm and compliance blogs; I did not check the Official Journal). It enters into force on 27 July 2026, before 2 August, and moves the Annex III date to 2 December 2027. So 2 August 2026 is the legal answer for 20 July, but in practice the obligations will apply from 2 December 2027.

parsed.quote: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on their behalf
parsed.answer: No. Article 4 is a best-efforts obligation. Providers and deployers must take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy. It does not guarantee a specific level for each staff member. If the proposed Omnibus amendment has been adopted, the duty would be weakened further, not strengthened.

Strict conditions apply: other data, such as synthetic or anonymised data, must not work; the data must be pseudonymised, kept secure and not shared; it must be deleted once the bias is corrected; and the reasons must be recorded. parsed.quote: AI systems that constitute or that are integrated into a very large online platform or very large online search engine designated in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2022/2065.
parsed.answer: The AI Office has exclusive competence. In the consolidated text as amended by the Omnibus, Article 75(1) makes the AI Office "exclusively competent for the supervision and enforcement" of the Regulation's obligations for AI systems that are, or are part of, a very large online platform or search engine designated under the Digital Services Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/2065). parsed.answer: No. Under Article 3(14), as amended by the Omnibus (Regulation 2026/1744), a component fulfils a safety function only if its intended purpose is to prevent or mitigate risks to the health and safety of persons or property. An AI system used only for convenience or quality control does not have that purpose, so it does not fulfil a safety function. One caveat: the definition has a second test. A component still counts as a safety component if its failure or malfunctioning endangers the health and safety of persons or property. If that is not the case, the system is not a safety component.

parsed.version: 02024R1689-20260727 (consolidated, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Omnibus)
parsed.quote: This obligation does not require providers or deployers to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of any individual.
parsed.answer: No. As amended by the Omnibus, Article 4(1) requires providers and deployers to take measures to support the development of AI literacy among their staff and other persons who operate or use AI systems on their behalf. This must take account of those people's knowledge, experience, education and training, the context of use, and the people the systems are used on. Under Article 4(2), the Commission and Member States must support these efforts, especially for SMEs, including by publishing practical examples.

parsed.answer: The original AI Act gives no authority exclusive competence over AI systems integrated into designated VLOPs. Article 75(1) gives the AI Office powers only over AI systems based on a GPAI model where the same provider developed both. Otherwise, national market surveillance authorities supervise. The Commission's Digital Omnibus proposal (November 2025) would make the AI Office exclusively competent for AI systems that are, or are integrated into, DSA-designated VLOPs and VLOSEs. Check whether that amendment has been adopted and is in force before relying on it.

raw: {"date":"2026-12-02","version":"Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744","article":"Article 5(1a)","quote":"a reasonably foreseeable and reproducible outcome","answer":"The limit is in Article 5(1a), added by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). The Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, added this ban and the related ban in point (bb). The Omnibus came into force on 27 July 2026. Its amended Article 113 sets the later start date of 2 December 2026 for points (ba) and (bb). The other Article 5 prohibitions have applied since 2 February 2025. I took this from secondary sources: artificialintelligenceact.eu (https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/ai-act-explorer/digital-omnibus/) and vorplabs.com. I did not check it against the Official Journal text.

I could not check the amended text itself, so I have not given a quotation.

parsed.answer: The answer is Article 4a. The Digital Omnibus (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) moved this rule out of the original Article 10(5) and into a new Article 4a. As of 5 October 2026, Article 4a(1) lets providers of high-risk AI systems exceptionally process special categories of personal data. This is allowed only where strictly necessary to detect and correct bias under Article 10(2)(f) and (g), and only if all the conditions in points (a) to (f) are met. Those conditions include that other data, such as synthetic or anonymised data, would not do the job, that the data is pseudonymised and access is restricted, and that it is deleted afterwards. Article 4a(2) gives a similar permission to deployers and to other AI systems and models.

parsed.quote: Where an AI system is based on a general-purpose AI model, and the model and the system are developed by the same provider, the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system with obligations under this Regulation.
parsed.answer: The original AI Act gives no authority exclusive competence for AI systems integrated into DSA-designated very large online platforms. Article 75(1) covers only AI systems built on a provider's own general-purpose AI model, and gives the AI Office monitoring powers there. Otherwise, national market surveillance authorities supervise under Article 74. The Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI (proposed November 2025) would amend Article 75 to make the AI Office exclusively competent for AI systems that are, or are integrated into, VLOPs or VLOSEs. If that amendment has been adopted and is in force, the answer is the AI Office. I cannot verify its adoption as of this date.

In the consolidated version in force on 2026-10-05, after the Omnibus amendment (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), the third sentence of Article 72(3) uses exactly this wording. The Commission must adopt guidance on the post-market monitoring plan, including a template, by 2 September 2027. The quote leaves out the paragraph's first two sentences. Those sentences say the post-market monitoring system is based on the plan and that the plan forms part of the Annex IV technical documentation. Only the Official Journal text is legally authentic.

parsed.version: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
parsed.quote: design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make that outcome reasonably foreseeable and reproducible without significant technical modification
parsed.answer: The provision is Article 5(1a). Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 inserted it, together with new Article 5(1), first subparagraph, points (ba) and (bb). Under Article 5(1a), providers are caught by the ban on placing these systems on the market only in two cases. The first is where generating or manipulating intimate or sexually explicit material is the system's intended purpose. The second is where the system's design, training, architecture, capabilities or user-facing functionalities make that outcome reasonably foreseeable and reproducible without significant technical modification, and the system lacks adequate safeguards. Deployers are caught where they use the system to generate such material. On 5 October 2026 the amendment is in force (since 27 July 2026), but this ban only applies from 2 December 2026. The quote comes from a secondary summary, not the Official Journal text.
